guides.favoredWhen: She short-trades after plating and TP-answers your R, but past early she cannot kill you. Stack armor, scale.

keyTips.text: Bone Plating plus RoA (sometimes Mercs) make you too tanky: low cooldowns give high DPS, so force extended trades.
She short-trades only after Bone Plating is gone: your plating gates every trade.
Past early she will not kill you unless far ahead: concede nothing, scale everything.

tips.text: She waits out Bone Plating: trade into her patience.
She keeps E for your chase: never chase into a held chain.
She always TPs to answer your R: R where her TP cannot follow.
Her E answers your chase: sidestep the chain, run her down.
Tanky plus scaling: the LeBlanc who never got ahead never kills you.

guides.favoredWhen: One of the best for two seasons. Push her in, mark minions, spread Q into shroud.

keyTips.text: One of the worst for her, best for you: press the pick, not just the player.
Early you push her in: her tower is her only safety, so crash.
Your Q spreads into shroud: stealth does not save her.

tips.text: She avoids minions with your E mark: marked waves explode, so mark them.
She farms the crash: pushed-in CS is safe CS, so deny it.
Your trade pattern plus defensive mage items decide it: force stat-checks.
She all-ins only on cooldown gaps: your pattern has holes, hide them.
Pushed in plus marked: the Akali who never dodged never wins.

sources.author: Anguish333
sources.rankClaim: Master (profile badge; title claims 2000LP GrandMaster EUW and Challenger EUNE) · Akali main

keyTips.text: Rush Seraph's Embrace instead of Rod of Ages for earlier damage and ability haste with its shield as protection, stacking Tear of the Goddess toward completion around twelve to thirteen minutes.
Respect the weak early levels: avoid treating pre-Seraph's trades as guaranteed wins, push and roam only when the opponent permits it, and coordinate those moves with the jungler around objectives.
After Seraph's and Fimbulwinter, Ryze survives longer and can win some one-versus-two fights against unfed opponents; treat that durability as a build-dependent claim, not a reason to force fights.

tips.text: Use E early to build Tear and Manaflow Band stacks while staying safe.
Shove and take the pre-level-six bot roam behind Dragon pit with enemy-jungle vision when the lane allows it, rather than sitting mid with no plan.
Treat the level-six Realm Warp unlock as the cross-map spike: after a recall, look for a fast ult to mid or top instead of walking back to lane on autopilot.
Open Tear of the Goddess with two Health Potions to start the stacking clock immediately.
Work with the jungler for picks, or take a side lane when the map allows safe collection.
At the Seraph's plus Fimbulwinter durability spike, reported around three thousand health plus the Seraph's shield near eighteen minutes, Ryze can hold riskier positions.
In the late game, choose between side-lane pressure that pulls enemies off your team, grouping mid for picks before objectives, or a flank onto squishy carries.
Use Realm Warp to reach lanes or create an unexpected flank, but staying alive for the late fights matters more than the flashy angle.
Treat Actualizer as the late one-versus-two multiplier on the Q-W-E-Q combo, using it as a power spike rather than an excuse to fight while behind.

itemization.text: Run Stormraider's Surge with Manaflow Band, Transcendence, Gathering Storm, Cash Back, and Cosmic Insight; open Tear and potions, then prioritize Lucidity boots with Seraph's, Fimbulwinter, Actualizer, and Rabadon's Deathcap.

Take Blackfire Torch as a late option and Warmog's Armor, Frozen Heart, Zhonya's Hourglass, Cryptbloom, or Cosmic Drive for the last slot; the alternate Rod of Ages route exists, though Seraph's first gives earlier haste and damage.
